public_rationale: The Imprompter paper, archived on October 19, 2024, demonstrates that obfuscated prompts made tested LLM agents extract personal information and transmit it externally through Markdown image requests [e1]. WIRED disclosed the research on October 17, 2024, and reported that Mistral had blocked external image loading to address the vulnerability [e2]. This supports the claimed capability in tested systems; the reported remediation does not negate the experimental demonstration [e1, e2].
limitations: The evidence does not establish that every LLM is vulnerable or that tested products remain vulnerable after remediation [e1, e2].
The demonstration does not establish a real-world criminal breach [e1, e2].
Using a short prompt does not establish that constructing the optimized prompt was simple [e2].
Exact experiment dates are unspecified; October 2024 identifies the research disclosure, and the archived paper appeared two days after the post [e1, e2].

evidence.explanation: The paper demonstrates extraction of personal information and transmission through Markdown image requests in tested agents. Its archived version appeared October 19; contemporaneous reporting in e2 establishes that this research had already been disclosed on October 17.

The article documents the research's public disclosure and reports that Mistral blocked external image loading, with researcher confirmation. This limits any implication of continuing vulnerability in that product; a separately accessible primary remediation notice was not found.
